findings.title: 813 flow(s) report more payload bytes than wire bytes across 3 class(es); dos materially affected
findings.detail: Payload bytes are a subset of the bytes that crossed the wire, so a flow where orig_bytes exceeds orig_ip_bytes (or resp_bytes exceeds resp_ip_bytes) is arithmetically impossible: Zeek derives the first from TCP sequence numbers, which wrap on scan and RST traffic, and counts the second off the wire, which cannot. These are the same columns that carry the largest label correlation in 2017 (point-biserial -0.442) and the largest attack-class mutual information (0.835), so the corruption sits exactly where the label signal is and every expectation or model built on it inherits the wrap. Use orig_ip_bytes and resp_ip_bytes instead.

SELECT label_class, count(*) AS n, sum(CASE WHEN "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes" OR "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), sum(CASE WHEN "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), max("orig_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes"), max("orig_ip_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes"), max("orig_bytes" / nullif("orig_pkts", 0)) FILTER (WHERE "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes"), arg_max(uid, "orig_bytes" - "orig_ip_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "orig_bytes" > "orig_ip_bytes"), sum(CASE WHEN "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), max("resp_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes"), max("resp_ip_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes"), max("resp_bytes" / nullif("resp_pkts", 0)) FILTER (WHERE "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes"), arg_max(uid, "resp_bytes" - "resp_ip_bytes") FILTER (WHERE "resp_bytes" > "resp_ip_bytes")

findings.title: 3,475 benign flow(s) are attacks according to the external oracle, 6,276 of them in 3 window(s) CIC is known to have got wrong
findings.detail: These flows carry no rule match, so they are benign only because the published schedule does not mention them -- and an independent manual re-labelling of the same packets says an attack was running. Every one is currently training data for the benign class. 6,276 of them fall inside a window the CNS2022 forensics already established that CIC mislabelled (Botnet Ares failed-C2 tail, Infiltration Cool Disk - MAC, Infiltration NMAP scan, early start), where the fault is ours by inheritance: the transcription is faithful and the source schedule is wrong. The correction belongs in the manifest. A further 5,095 flow(s) match only `- Attempted` oracle rows and are excluded from the count above: an attempt that delivered nothing is a defensible thing to call benign.

findings.title: dos/DoS-Slowhttptest misses 1 of 5 behavioural expectation(s), worst by 31.2%
findings.detail: The flows carrying this label do not behave the way the label names. Either the window is over the wrong traffic, or the band in expectations.yaml is wrong -- the measured rate and the floor it missed are both reported so the reader can tell which.

evidence.why: The whole point of the attack is to exhaust a web server's connection pool. A slow-DoS window whose traffic is on another port is a window over the wrong traffic -- this is the band that fails on 2018, where 105,550 flows in the dos class sit on port 21.
Partial headers, dripped. Never a full request.
The socket is held, not fed. PROVISIONAL -- the profile pools the slow and fast DoS variants, so this is reasoned rather than measured.
PROVISIONAL, and the floor is deliberately low. Slow-DoS connections that are still open when the capture ends are logged by Zeek with a truncated duration, so this cannot be asserted strongly.
Single-source by definition, so the flow count per source host is what separates dos from ddos.

       sum(CASE WHEN (coalesce(duration, 0) >= 5.0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS held_open
FROM read_parquet('s3://ids-datalakec48eb2cab942494ba5059fac3b3527d9/labelled/cic-ids-2017/**/*.parquet', union_by_name=true)
WHERE label_class = 'dos' AND label_raw = 'DoS-Slowhttptest'

findings.title: duration is null for 8.10% of dos flows
findings.detail: 37,090 flow(s) carry no duration. The EDA spec coalesces this feature's nulls to 0, so those flows are indistinguishable from flows that genuinely measured zero, and a class whose zero mass is really missing data will look flood-shaped whether or not it is. Nothing here says the labels are wrong -- it constrains which features a downstream claim about the affected classes may rest on, and requires that nulls be excluded explicitly rather than read as zeros.

findings.title: CICFlowMeter artefact probes ran over 2,119,182 flows and found none of the signatures
findings.detail: Reported because the negative result is the finding. Rosay et al. (ICISSP 2022) identified four artefact classes that CICFlowMeter writes into every CSV it generates -- constant bulk features from an integer division, ARP frames read as IPv4 traffic between 8.0.6.4 and 8.6.0.1, non-TCP/UDP packets collapsed to protocol 0 with ports 0, and TCP flows cut at the first FIN whose halves can end up labelled differently -- and stated that every dataset shipping CICFlowMeter CSVs carries them, CIC-IDS-2017, CSE-CIC-IDS-2018 and CIC-DDoS-2019 included. Talos does not use those CSVs; the lake is Zeek output over the original pcaps. This check is the measurement behind that claim, so that 'our features do not carry the published artefacts' is a reading rather than an assertion. Probe 1 has no literal equivalent in Zeek's schema and is reported as inapplicable rather than faked.

findings.title: 6,306 of 2,114,093 oracle matches (0.30%) have the originator reversed
findings.detail: CICFlowMeter fixes direction from the first packet it sees and Zeek from the SYN, so the two disagree wherever a handshake is absent. The join keys on the unordered 5-tuple precisely so these flows are matched instead of lost, and this is the measurement that would otherwise be invisible. It indicts neither labelling. It does bound the rest of the tier -- agreement is computed over direction-agreeing matches only -- and it means any orig/resp-relative feature is not describing the same endpoint on both sides.
